price_per_million.source: copied from reasoning_models_v1 (confirmed 2026-11-11); thinking tokens billed as output

research_concepts: cut share vs drive share (play-type mix)
role portability across teams (post-move reproduction of function)
methodological_questions: What counts as a 'shaper', and is it the same as the 'connector' used in prior work?
How is 'travels better' measured, and is the portability Delta reliable at n=24?
Can cut-heavy and drive-heavy shapers be separated from teammate, scheme and menu-similarity confounds?
How much does play-type label error affect cut and drive shares?
Is a result from n=24 powered, or only an estimate of effect size?

historical_evidence.finding: Among 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted portability: rho=+0.265, p=0.011, AUC 0.653. Drive share was negatively related: rho=-0.278, p=0.007. The top cut tercile was 65% portable (median Delta +0.167) versus a bottom-tercile median of -0.039. Leave-one-out AUC was 0.622 and the permutation p was 0.005. The result held after dropping Gafford (rho=+0.244, p=0.020). Notes say the scripts were exploratory, validation was same-pipeline, and almost all other pre-move predictors were null.

Movers' displacement signatures were more similar across franchises than profile-matched decoys' (median Delta=+0.0557, perm p=0.005, 173/294 positive). This supports portability in general, not the cut-vs-drive contrast.

In connector-mover pairing variants (428 movers), the organizer-versus-connector gap had a CI including 0 after a menu-similarity confound was corrected. The KW p=0.047 was population-level, and pairwise differences were only suggestive.
The play-type label audit failed overall: OTHER was 20.2% against a <10% target, 40.8% of labels were low confidence, and DRIVE foul-draw was 1.7% against a 14-22% benchmark.
Connector absence displaces team offensive identity more than usage-matched role-player absence (n=96 pairs). This is relevant to connector function but does not address cut vs drive.
Replacement-profile similarity did not separate absorption from cascade (wrong-signed rho=-0.19). Similar-profile teammates were almost always findable.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Comparing connector subtypes on portability without controlling for menu similarity
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: confounding (menu-similarity) and small sample; the gap CI included 0 after correction.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Taking inferred play-type labels at face value, including DRIVE
failed_approaches.why: Recorded label or classification error, leakage and small sample; systematic label issues undermine findings built on play types.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Pooled play-type effects without within-team baselines
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: DRIVE lifts were flat and vanished within team (team-quality confound).

failed_approaches.what_failed: Global play-type lift analysis without team-season demeaning
failed_approaches.why: Recorded as artifact: global effects disappeared after team-season demeaning.

evidence_establishes: FAM:SF-CHT-057 reports that among 92 connector movers, higher pre-move cut share (and lower drive share) goes with better post-move reproduction of organizational function. It is recorded as supported, with exploratory origin and same-pipeline validation.
FAM:SF19 reports that movers' signatures travel beyond profile-matched decoys in general.
FAM:SF-CHT-087 records that a related organizer-vs-connector contrast did not survive a menu-similarity correction.
evidence_does_not_establish: That 'shapers' in this question are the same population as the 'connectors' in the prior work; the records do not say.
That the cut-vs-drive result replicates out of sample or on an independent n=24 unit set.

That the cut-drive association is independent of play-type label error, destination or scheme fit, and menu-similarity; CHT-057 records no such control, and CHT-087 shows a similar confound can erase a gap.
Any effect size or power for n=24.
own_inferences: The question looks like a restatement of the CHT-057 finding, so it is partly answered for connectors, but only in an exploratory, same-pipeline way.
At n=24, a true Spearman rho near 0.27 gives roughly 20-25% power, so a null would be uninformative and a significant result would probably overstate the effect.

Cut share and drive share are compositional and partly anti-correlated, so 'cut-heavy vs drive-heavy' may mostly measure one dimension. The DRIVE label is the weakest, since the foul-draw audit failed, so measurement error could attenuate or distort the contrast.
If the 24 units are a subset of the 92 connector movers or overlap with them, the test is not independent confirmation.
uncertainties: The definition of 'shaper' and how the 24 units were selected are not given.
Whether the 24 units overlap with prior samples is unknown.
The definition and reliability of the 'travels' outcome (Delta) at the individual-player level are not given.
Whether 2025-26 data entered the earlier analyses is unknown (CHT-057 is dated 2026-07-19).
Whether 2025-26 data, partial before the dates given, is complete enough to define post-move windows.

historical_effect.explanation: Without history I would have treated this as a new directional test. The history shows a prior supported but exploratory connector result and a related artifact caused by confounding, which shifted the plan to a pre-registered, confound-controlled replication reported as estimation, with no confirmatory claim at n=24 alone.

blocking_constraints.text: n=24 gives low power for a rho of about 0.27, and a tercile split would leave about 8 units per group.
The play-type audit failed, and DRIVE is especially poorly labelled, so cut and drive shares carry measurement error.
Destination scheme, teammate menu similarity and usage are not controlled in the earlier cut-drive result.

prior_work.summary: For connectors, CHT-057 reports a supported but exploratory cut-over-drive portability association (n=92). It is not independent replication, and confounding and label-quality concerns are on record. The 'shaper' framing and n=24 are not covered by any retrieved record.

risks.text: n=24 is underpowered. A null would not reject the hypothesis, and a significant result would likely be inflated (winner's curse).
Inferred cut and drive labels are error-prone (APPM-014), so shares are noisy.
Destination menu similarity, scheme, usage and teammate quality can mimic differences in portability (CHT-087).
The player-level portability Delta may be unreliable with few post-move possessions.
CHT-057 notes almost all other predictors were null and the scripts were exploratory, so the cut-share finding may be a forking-paths pick.
Extreme cut-heavy or drive-heavy units selected on pre-move profile may regress to the mean.
Few cut or drive actions per mover in short post-move windows make the shares unstable.
Four seasons with rules and league-style change, and partial 2025-26 data, make windows non-comparable.

design.estimand: Association (Spearman rho and a rank-based AUC) between pre-move cut share minus drive share and post-move portability Delta (profile-matched-decoy-adjusted signature similarity, as in SF19/CHT-057), with an effect-size CI. Directional hypothesis: rho > 0.
design.unit: One mover (player-move event) classified as a shaper under a fixed definition, written down before analysis. Report overlap with the 92 CHT-057 movers.
design.sample: The 24 recorded units from 2022-23 to 2025-26. Include 2025-26 data only from the dates marked complete. Pre-register inclusion thresholds (minimum possessions pre and post, minimum number of decoys). Mark units that overlap CHT-057 and report results with and without them; only non-overlapping units count as independent replication.
design.power: At n=24 and alpha=0.05 one-sided, power is about 0.2-0.3 for rho=0.27 and about 0.6 for rho=0.5. Report this up front. Primary reporting is the effect size with a bootstrap CI. A null cannot reject; significance alone is not confirmation. Prefer pooling with the 92 CHT-057 movers (hierarchical or stratified) only for estimation and clearly label it.
design.controls: Include destination menu similarity (per CHT-087), usage rate, minutes, destination-team cut and drive rates, and position as covariates. Use partial-rank or regression with robust SEs. Use profile-matched decoys. Cluster by destination franchise. Check label sensitivity by restricting to high-confidence play-type labels and excluding OTHER or foul-leaked possessions.
design.falsification: Permute portability labels (5000 shuffles). Run a placebo using a non-role predictor (for example a spot-up share) that CHT-057 found null. Run a leave-one-out analysis. Treat a CI that includes 0 or a sign flip under the label-quality filter as a failure to replicate.
design.multiplicity: A single primary test (cut minus drive share vs Delta). Secondary analyses (cut alone, drive alone, terciles, position splits) are labelled exploratory and use Holm correction.
design.decision_rule: Supported only if the one-sided permutation p<0.05, the bootstrap CI for rho excludes 0, the sign is stable under the label-quality filter, and the estimate holds after controlling for menu similarity. If rho>0 but the CI includes 0, report 'inconclusive, underpowered'. If the sign reverses or the confound removes the effect, report 'not replicated or artifact'. No confirmatory claim from n=24 alone.
design.data_version: NBA stats API per-game files for 2022-23 to 2024-25 (full), 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13) and playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21), plus the play-type possession records. Freeze the dataset snapshot and labelling pipeline version, and the shaper definition and move list, before any analysis.

methodological_questions: How is role portability defined and measured when players change teams or lineups?
Are role classifications reliable and stable across seasons with small samples (n=24 units)?
How to separate role travel from teammate, scheme, and usage confounding?
Does regression to the mean or selection of movers bias portability comparisons?
Is play-type labelling derived from outcomes or from play-by-play inference with label error?
args.query: Do cut-heavy shapers retain their role after changing team or context better than drive-heavy shapers? Role portability, role persistence, play-type based role classification from play-by-play, small sample of 24 units.

system_prompt:
You are a basketball analytics researcher deciding whether and how a research question should be studied.
You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.
Stage 1, retrieval:
1. Read the research objective and the data description.
2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.
3. Retrieve historical evidence by calling retrieve_history.
In stage 1 do not assess the question, predict outcomes or decide. Your only stage-1 reply is the retrieve_history call.
Stage 2, assessment, after the retrieval result is returned:
4. Summarise the relevant historical findings and failed approaches.
5. State what the historical evidence does and does not establish.
6. Assess whether the research question is testable.
7. Identify methodological risks and potential confounders.
8. Make the final research decision.
9. Explain whether and how the historical evidence changed the decision.
The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

Evidence rules: keep what a retrieved record states (historical_evidence and failed_approaches, each citing the
identifier of a returned record and its status exactly as recorded) separate from your own inference and from
uncertainty or missing information. Cite only identifiers returned by a tool, and never describe an earlier study that
no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Tools:
- retrieve_history(research_concepts, methodological_questions, query): the prescribed retrieval step. Returns the most relevant consolidated study-family records of earlier research by this project that are available in this setting, with their identifiers; returns an empty list when none are available.
- glossary(): definitions of basketball and project terms used in task statements.
- data_catalog(): the fields available in each per-game data file.
- search_documents(query): rank further study-family documents by text relevance; returns up to 10 families not yet returned.
- read_family(id): the complete record of one study family (for example 'FAM:SF-APPA-001').

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.

Risk codes (use only these): SAMPLE_SIZE_POWER, EXPOSURE_SPARSITY, MEASURE_RELIABILITY, RTM_SELECTION, OUTCOME_DERIVED_LABEL, LEAKAGE_LOOKAHEAD, MECHANICAL_FLOOR, BASE_RATE, CONFOUNDING, LABEL_ERROR, PLACEBO_DEPENDENCE, MULTIPLE_TESTING, IMPLEMENTATION_BUG, DRIFT_NONSTATIONARITY

Research question (as posed on 2026-08-08, in the area of structural roles and influence):
Cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones.

Data available on that date:
- NBA 2022-23 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2023-24 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2024-25 regular season and playoffs
- NBA 2025-26 regular season (complete from 2026-04-13; partial before)
- NBA 2025-26 playoffs (complete from 2026-06-21; partial before)
- Sources: Per-game files from the NBA stats API: play-by-play (action type, sub-type, clock, period, score, player, shot distance and result), substitution rotation intervals, starters, defensive matchup minutes and partial possessions, box-score summary. Derived play-type possession records (initiator, play type, points) in a graph database built from the play-by-play.
- Units available to a study of this question (as recorded): n=24

Your job is to decide, before any analysis is run, whether this question can be answered with this data, what has already been established about it, which methodological and statistical risks threaten a test of it, and either a pre-registration-quality design or a reasoned recommendation not to proceed.

Stage 1. Reply only with the retrieval call: {"action": "tool", "tool": "retrieve_history", "args": {"research_concepts": ["..."], "methodological_questions": ["..."], "query": "..."}}

reasoning_details.text:
I'm settling on the final call now: the question is whether cut-heavy shapers' roles travel better than drive-heavy ones, with only 24 units. Prior work covered 92 connector movers, not shapers, so it only partly speaks to this and I shouldn't overstate it. With a sample this small the power is low, and the Spearman rho sits near zero, so I'm weighing whether to proceed with changes or not proceed at all.

I'm leaning toward proceeding with changes: treat this as a pooled out-of-sample replication of the prior rule, with the 2025-26 data and a clear note that power is low and the effect size should come with a confidence interval. I'd rather frame it that way than as a standalone confirmatory test on 24 units. I also need to check whether the prior work already included the 2025-26 season, because that affects whether the replication is truly independent.
